name: BQ25040DQCR
title: 1.1 A single-cell Li-ion linear charger with 50 mA LDO and 2.3 A production test mode
summary: The bq25040 is a linear charger for one Li-ion cell, fed from a USB port or a wall adapter, with up to 1.1 A of charge current in a 2 mm × 3 mm 10-pin SON. A single pulse-coded pin, EN/SET, switches it on and off and picks USB100, USB500 or a resistor-set current, or a production test mode in which BAT holds 4.2 V and delivers up to 2.3 A with no cell fitted. It also carries a 4.9 V, 50 mA LDO, a 30 V-rated input with overvoltage cut-off at 6.9 V, input-voltage DPM, thermal regulation, and two open-drain flags, PG and CHG.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply from the adapter or USB VBUS. Decouple to VSS with 1 µF ceramic or more.

pins.name: ISET
pins.function: A resistor to VSS (475 Ω to 5.36 kΩ) sets the fast-charge current from 100 mA to 1.1 A in the user-programmed mode. When the ISET current is below the USB500 limit, it also caps the current in USB500 mode.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Ground. Tie to the exposed pad and the board ground plane.

pins.name: LDO
pins.function: 4.9 V regulator output, up to 50 mA, on whenever VIN is above UVLO and below VOVP. Needs 1 µF ceramic or more to VSS. Its current is outside the input current limit.

pins.name: IFULL
pins.function: A resistor to VSS sets the charge-done level, 5 % to 50 % of the ISET current. CHG turns high-impedance once IBAT drops to that level.

pins.name: EN/SET
pins.function: One-wire control: pulse trains turn the IC on or off and choose the mode. An internal pull-down of about 260 kΩ holds it at VSS.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Ground, the same node as pin 3.

pins.name: CHG
pins.function: Low while a charge is in progress; released to high impedance when the cell is full and stays so through later top-up charges. Also high impedance under a fault.

pins.name: PG
pins.function: Low while VIN is at least 80 mV above VBAT and below the OVP threshold; high impedance otherwise.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Charger output to the cell and the system load. Needs 1 µF ceramic or more to VSS, and at least 40 µF with no cell fitted. In production test mode it holds 4.2 V and sources up to 2.3 A.

pins.name: Thermal pad
pins.function: Exposed pad, joined to VSS inside the package. Solder it to the VSS potential on the board, but keep the VSS pins wired to ground as the main ground return at all times.

circuits.title: Application schematic, adapter or USB input
circuits.description: The charger is fed either from an adapter or from a USB port's VBUS, both landing on IN with C1 (1 µF). R1 (680 Ω) on ISET gives about 780 mA of fast charge and R2 (2 kΩ) on IFULL sets charge-done at 10 % of that. BAT feeds the cell, C2 and the baseband processor (ABB); two LEDs with 1 kΩ resistors hang from BAT onto the open-drain PG and CHG pins. The ABB drives EN/SET, takes the 4.9 V LDO output (decoupled by C3) and the USB data lines.
notes: Only one of the two sources is connected at a time.

circuits.title: Typical application with the battery always fitted, ICHRG = 780 mA, ICHGDONE = 78 mA
circuits.description: A USB port or travel adapter feeds IN, bypassed by C1 (1 µF); its data lines are left open. R1 (680 Ω) sets about 780 mA of fast charge and R2 (2 kΩ) a 10 % charge-done level. BAT goes to the cell, to C2 (1 µF) and to the ABB's VCHG input, and supplies two LEDs through 1 kΩ resistors that sink into PG and CHG. A GPIO of the ABB drives EN/SET. The LDO output, with C3 (1 µF), feeds the ABB's VCHG DET, USB DET and VUSBIN pins.

circuits.title: Typical application for PTM or with no battery fitted, ICHRG = 780 mA, ICHGDONE = 39 mA
circuits.description: The same wiring as the battery-fitted circuit, with two changes for running the system without a cell or in production test mode: C1 on IN grows to 22 µF, and the system side of BAT carries bulk capacitance of more than 40 µF (CB1, CB2) besides C2 (1 µF). The cell position BT1 is empty during PTM.

operation.text: A charge begins once three things hold: a cell below the recharge level is on BAT, EN/SET is low, and the input is valid. Valid means VIN above UVLO, more than 80 mV over VBAT and under VOVP.

Below VLOWV (2.5 V) the cell gets a pre-charge current of 20 % of the ISET setting. Above VLOWV the fast-charge limit chosen through EN/SET (USB100, USB500 or ISET) applies. On reaching VBAT(REG) the charger holds the voltage while the current tapers. When IBAT falls to the IFULL level, CHG is released but charging carries on. There are no safety timers in the IC; the host has to time the charge.
In every phase the junction temperature is watched, and the charge current is cut back when it passes the internal limit.
Pulling EN/SET low enables the IC. After a 50 µs deglitch it waits 32 ms (tWAIT), during which a mode can be pulsed in; with no pulses the IC comes up in USB500 mode.

Each high pulse and each gap between pulses must last 100 µs to 700 µs. The count is decoded once EN/SET has stayed low for 1.5 ms. A fourth pulse selects USB100 at once without waiting for the 1.5 ms timer. After one mode is set, further pulses are ignored until the input power is cycled or the IC is disabled and re-enabled.
Holding EN/SET high for longer than 1.5 ms disables the IC: charging stops and input quiescent current drops. The LDO is not controlled by EN/SET.

EN/SET chooses USB100, USB500 or the ISET current. If the ISET current is set lower than the USB500 limit, it is the ISET value that applies in USB500 mode. Pre-charge is always 20 % of the ISET current, not of the selected mode, though in USB100 mode it can be held to the USB100 limit.

IFULL% is a share of the ISET fast-charge current and must lie from 5 % to 50 %. CHG goes high when IBAT drops below it, telling the host to end the cycle; the IC itself keeps charging until EN/SET disables it.

Three pulses on EN/SET select PTM: BAT is regulated to 4.2 V and can supply up to 2.3 A with no cell fitted, for powering a product on a test line. It cannot carry 2.3 A continuously; above 1.5 A the user has to hold the full-current duty cycle to 20 %, with a period of 10 ms or less. Thermal regulation is off in PTM; thermal shutdown stays active.
Below UVLO the IC sits in power-down: EN/SET is ignored, the pass FET from IN to BAT stays off, and PG and CHG float. Above UVLO it starts normally.

Above VOVP both the LDO and the charger shut off. A 115 µs blanking time rides through input ringing. An adapter that is above VOVP at plug-in sees the IC finish its soft start, then shut down if the input is still high after 115 µs; it stays off until VIN drops below VOVP.

In USB100 and USB500 modes the input voltage is watched; should it drop as far as VIN(DPM), the IC trims its input current so the source is not pulled down further. This keeps a weak or wrongly configured USB source from collapsing, for example a 250 mA-limited source with USB500 (395 mA) selected.

The LDO gives up to 50 mA at VLDO whenever VIN is between UVLO and VOVP, regardless of EN/SET, for loads such as a USB transceiver that must run while the cell is flat. Its current has its own limit and adds to the input current limit; thermal regulation does not reduce it.

Open drain, pulled to VSS during pre-charge, fast charge and CV. It goes high impedance once the output is in regulation and the current is below the termination level, and stays high through later refresh charges. For a microcontroller input, pull it up through 1 kΩ to 100 kΩ; it can also drive an LED at under 15 mA. The pull-up rail may be anything under the pin rating. An LED pulled up to the cell dims at low battery; pulled up to LDO, its current is outside the input limit and can push the input past the USB100 maximum.
Open drain, low when the input lies between VBAT + 80 mV and VOVP and is above UVLO. Pull-up choices behave as for CHG. Each input event has its own nominal PG deglitch time, enabled or disabled.

Above TJ(REG) the charge current is reduced to hold the die temperature. If the die still reaches TJ(OFF) the charge FET turns off, and turns on again after cooling by TJ(OFF-HYS); a lasting overtemperature makes the load current pulse. These loops act on die temperature, not ambient. Battery temperature (NTC) has to be watched by the host.

IN: 1 µF ceramic close to IN and the ground pad for normal charging; 22 µF for PTM at up to 2.3 A; more where cable and source ringing at hot plug could exceed the OVP level for longer than the deglitch. BAT: 1 µF ceramic close to the pins for loop stability; 40 µF for PTM up to 2.3 A; more to limit droop on large load steps. LDO: at least 1 µF ceramic close to the pins, larger for better transient response.

PG and CHG are 7 V open-drain FETs. Pull them up to the host supply when a host reads them. For LEDs the supply can be BAT, LDO or IN. From IN, a 6.2 V zener clamp is needed if the input can exceed 7 V. From BAT, brightness follows the cell and falls sharply below 3 V. LDO is a regulated rail and suits LEDs at high input voltage.

The exposed pad carries heat into the board; θJA depends on mounting, trace size and copper, orientation, air volume and flow, and nearby surfaces. With weak board thermal design the thermal loop may cut the programmed charge current at high input voltage and low cell voltage.

Put the IN and BAT capacitors as close to the IC as possible, with short traces to IN, BAT and the ground pad. Keep low-current grounds apart from the battery's high-current paths and join the two at a single point. Size the IN and BAT traces for the full charge current. Solder the exposed pad to board ground: it doubles as the IC's principal ground path.
